findings.title: `_source` is returned with raw encrypted attributes whenever the `_id` column is missing.
findings.body: `decryptSourceColumn` returns the response unchanged when the `_id` column is absent. This happens with `metadata: ['_source']`, or with `metadata: ['_id','_source']` plus `| DROP _id` / `| KEEP _source`. `stripEncryptedColumns` only nulls `<type>.<attr>` columns and never touches the `_source` object, so encrypted attribute ciphertext (and attributes `find` would strip) goes back to the caller unchanged. The same happens when a row's `_id` is null or the pipeline renames `_source`. This breaks the stated guarantee that encrypted attributes are decrypted or stripped. Fix: when `_source` is present and decryption cannot be attempted, remove the type's encrypted attributes (`getEncryptedAttributes`) from `source[docType]`. Alternatively, reject queries that return `_source` without `_id`.

findings.title: The rebuilt saved object uses the raw ES `_id` and drops `namespace`, so `_source` decryption always fails.
findings.body: The ES|QL `_id` metadata column holds the raw document id. Its format is `<type>:<id>`, or `<namespace>:<type>:<id>` for single-namespace types in a non-default space. The code passes that value as `SavedObject.id`. Single-namespace documents also store `namespace` (singular) in `_source`, but only `namespaces` is copied here. The AAD that `decryptOrStripResponseAttributes` builds therefore never matches the one used at encryption time. Every row fails to decrypt, gets stripped, and logs a decryption error. The feature documented in the tutorial ("Encrypted attributes are **decrypted** in `_source` using the same path as `find`") never works. The unit tests miss this because they mock the extension. Fix: convert the raw id with the serializer (`serializer.rawToSavedObject` or by parsing the id), and pass `namespace` for single-namespace types before calling the extension.

findings.title: The agent's working files (`tasks/prd.json`, `tasks/progress.txt`) are committed to the repository root.
findings.body: These are scratch files from an autonomous agent loop ("Ralph Progress Log", the user-story checklist with `passes` flags, branch names). They are not part of the feature and the request does not ask for them. They add a new top-level `tasks/` directory to Kibana and would ship with the source. Remove both files from the PR.

findings.title: The pipeline is not required to start with `|`, so callers can add indices to the generated FROM clause.
findings.body: The only check is a regex that rejects a leading source command. A pipeline such as `, .some-other-index* | LIMIT 10` or `, remote:* | ...` passes the check. It produces `FROM .kibana_x, .some-other-index* | ...`, which runs as `kibana_system` against indices the `type` parameter was meant to control. The namespace/type `filter` limits which documents match, but index resolution is no longer controlled by the system as the PR claims. Any document in another index that has matching `type`/`namespace(s)` fields is returned. Fix: require the trimmed pipeline to be empty or start with `|`. Better, parse it with the ES|QL parser and reject anything that is not a processing command.
